title: Floor 4: The sample desk
card: A supervisor needs two trips to audit.
task: Create audit_sample with the two trips having the lowest row_id values, keeping every column.
guideTask: Create audit_sample with the two trips having the lowest row_id values, keeping every column.
context: The audit supervisor needs a small sample before reviewing the feed. trips holds the incoming trip rows and zones names their locations. Keeping two whole trips makes the sample useful for checking the original records.

refresher.title: Choose a small ordered sample
refresher.text: SELECT chooses columns, ORDER BY puts rows in a predictable order, and LIMIT keeps a small number. CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE saves that result and can be run again.
refresher.sql:
WITH notes(id) AS (VALUES (3), (1), (2))
SELECT * FROM notes ORDER BY id LIMIT 2;

summary: 4. The sample desk: keep the two incoming trips with the lowest physical row ids for an audit.
dirt: SELECT row_id, pu_location_id, do_location_id FROM trips ORDER BY row_id LIMIT 2
rulesText:
## Floor 4: The sample desk

Keep the two whole trips with the lowest row_id values in audit_sample.
taskContext: The audit supervisor needs two whole trips to check against the incoming feed.

levels: The task panel above Your SQL holds the full rules and a checklist for audit_sample. Open it before writing your query; it starts collapsed on mobile. The checklist says whether each table exists and counts its rows. Exists does not mean correct. SQL refresher and About the data links beside it open the guide in a new tab.

Use the task panel checklist after each Run: an empty audit_sample table still exists with zero rows. Replacing or dropping a table updates the count or marks it missing. Use Check this floor to test its rules. The panel remembers your collapse choice in the page address.

After CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE, compare the task panel checklist counts with your own SELECT count(*) queries on audit_sample. The checklist reports presence and size only; the full rules in the task panel explain what Check this floor will test.

Under Tables above Your SQL, open a table chip to see its columns and types. Start with trips to find the available names before writing a query. Opening a chip leaves your SQL and Result alone; Enter or Space opens and closes it from the keyboard.

The columns and types describe the table on the active floor, including tables you create. When you replace a table, an open chip refreshes its column view. After switching floors, open the new floor’s chip to inspect that floor’s columns and types.

Use the table chip’s columns and types to choose names for SELECT, WHERE and joins. The column view reads the table quietly: it adds no query to your history or the tutor’s recent queries and never replaces unfinished SQL.

Choose Preview beside any table chip under Tables to see its first 10 rows in a separate panel beside the console, or below it on a narrow screen. Start with trips to see what a row holds. Preview leaves Your SQL, Result and query records alone; Close preview takes you back to the chip.

Preview shows up to 10 rows from the table on this floor, including your own outputs. An empty table still shows its column names. Preview refreshes after a replacement and closes when you drop its table or change floors. The panel scrolls sideways for wide rows on a phone.

Preview is a quiet SELECT * with LIMIT 10, without a guaranteed sort order. It does not add a run to either query record. When a transaction is open, Preview explains that you must COMMIT or ROLLBACK before reading rows; it shows columns without running row expressions or changing your transaction.
